$comment: Claims ledger (charter rule 8). Every claim made in README.md/SPEC.md that is machine-checkable appears here with the exact command that verifies it. check-claims.sh runs each `check.cmd` with bash; exit 0 = claim holds. Two tiers (process rule 2): PR gate runs OFFLINE=1 (deterministic only); the live tier (live-checks.yml, nightly + manual dispatch) runs ONLINE_ONLY=1 and reports failures to a tracking issue instead of blocking merges. `online: true` claims hit live testnet and are skipped in the PR gate.

claims.claim: stellar-xdr is pinned to 28.0.1
the seed-testnet fixture contract builds against soroban-sdk 28.0.0
every committed seed-v2 upstream wasm fixture hashes exactly as recorded in scripts/upstream/upstream.lock.json

every contract id, deploy tx hash, deploy ledger, wasm sha256 and upstream SHA in deployments.json is backed by a committed raw RPC fixture and the pinned upstream.lock.json, and the registry contains no secret material
at least 85 tests pass across the workspace (unit + differential + property + dry-run)

check.cmd: n=$(cargo test --workspace 2>/dev/null | grep -oE 'ok\. [0-9]+ passed' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | awk '{s+=$1} END{print s+0}'); test "$n" -ge 85

claims.claim: the Script3 adapter's decoded state and tally equal the committed on-chain reads for every seeded proposal (ids 0-5), entirely offline
property tests cover zero votes, exact ties, i128 extremes, empty checkpoint history, exact-ledger hits and before-first-checkpoint lookups
the contextual risk rules treasury_outflow, self_call, large_value and batched_actions are published in risk.rs, each with a positive and a negative test

check.cmd: for r in treasury_outflow self_call large_value batched_actions; do grep -q "$r" crates/core/src/risk.rs || exit 1; done

claims.claim: the OpenZeppelin adapter is not implemented yet, matching the README honest limitation

the parser models simulateTransaction dry-run output from committed real captures, always estimate:true + a mandatory simulatedAtLedger, with absent fields null and cost fields null because no capture showed them
the v1 GraphQL SDL is unchanged or additive relative to the committed baseline (no type, field, argument or enum value removed or retyped)
README's stated WASM package sha256 and asset name match the committed release lock file, offline
the seed-v2 corpus holds 259 committed raw RPC responses and index.json lists exactly that many

check.cmd: n=$(ls tests/fixtures/seed-v2/rpc/*.json | wc -l); i=$(python3 -c "import json;print(len(json.load(open('tests/fixtures/seed-v2/index.json'))['fixtures']))"); test "$n" -eq 259 && test "$i" -eq 259

claims.claim: the wasm crate builds for wasm32-unknown-unknown (release)
SDF public testnet RPC reports ledgerRetentionWindow = 120960
the phase 1a fixture governor's events are still queryable on testnet (contract alive and its events within retention)

check.cmd: curl -sS --max-time 60 -X POST https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"getEvents","params":{"startLedger":5035900,"filters":[{"type":"contract","contractIds":["CDJWPKSQ4NA67PKTNJEPI6R2Q3JEDXPX5EDPM3YOSEHBDGBZ5THBTOKE"]}],"pagination":{"limit":5}}}' | jq -e '.result.events | length > 0'

claims.claim: the recorded live-testnet proof (tests/fixtures/phase1-proof.json) supports every fact in the README evidence table: retention window 120960, >=2 captured fixture events with 64-hex tx hashes, decoded proposal_created/vote_cast topics, live contractspecv0 with propose/vote/get_proposal, fail-closed negative proof on the SAC contract, >=23 unit tests, clippy clean
no production crate source references tests/fixtures

every github.com URL in tracked first-party files (including api.github.com/repos API URLs) points at the Stellar-Governance-Guardians org or an allow-listed upstream source citation (script3, OpenZeppelin — research provenance required by charter rule 3). Generated dependency lockfiles (package-lock.json) are excluded: their URLs are third-party registry metadata, not project references. The scan is restricted to `git ls-files` so untracked working-tree dirs (node_modules/) cannot affect it, matching CI.

check.cmd: ! (git ls-files -z -- '*.md' '*.json' '*.yml' '*.yaml' '*.toml' '*.graphql' | grep -zv 'package-lock\.json' | xargs -0 -r grep -Eoh 'https?://(api\.)?github\.com/(repos/)?[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+' 2>/dev/null | sed 's|https://api\.github\.com/repos/|https://github.com/|' | grep -vE '^https?://github\.com/(Stellar-Governance-Guardians|script3|OpenZeppelin)$' | grep -q .)

claims.claim: no personal GitHub account names appear in tracked files
risk classification is an exact-match published rule table; no composite/trust-score identifiers exist in the code (doc comments may discuss the concept)

check.cmd: grep -q 'pub static RULES' crates/core/src/risk.rs && ! grep -nE 'trust_score|trustScore|composite' crates/core/src/risk.rs | grep -vE '^[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*(//|/\*|\*)' | grep -q .

claims.claim: the CLI has a fail-closed ttl command reading protocol 29 instance/code TTL entries, with a min-remaining gate
